title: hubble_gradient.ipynb  -  Cosmological Test: Hubble Tension Resolution

canonical_node.axiom: The chi-field modifies the effective gravitational constant as G_eff(z) = G / (1 + chi(z)), producing a smooth sigmoid transition in the Hubble constant H(z) from a local value (H_local  73.5) at low redshift to a CMB value (H_CMB  67.4) at high redshift, with transition redshift z_transition  0.3.
definitions: chi-field: a scalar field chi(z) that varies with redshift, with chi -> 0 at high z and nonzero at low z.
G_eff(z): effective gravitational constant at redshift z, modified by the chi-field.
H(z): Hubble constant as a function of redshift, following a sigmoid profile.
5 match: statistical consistency at the 5-sigma level between the chi-field prediction and observational H measurements.
DESI DR2: Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 2, reporting 4.2 evidence for dark energy evolution.
derivation: The chi-field modifies gravity via G_eff(z) = G / (1 + chi(z)).
At high redshift, chi -> 0, so G_eff -> G, recovering standard gravity and Planck H.
At low redshift, chi is nonzero, suppressing G_eff and increasing the measured H.
The resulting H(z) follows a sigmoid: H(z) = H_CMB + (H_local  H_CMB) / (1 + exp(k(z  z_transition))).
The chi-field parameters are set by the Lagrangian, not fitted to the Hubble data.
The prediction is compared to observational data, yielding a 5 match.
The chi-field also produces a slowly varying effective dark energy, compatible with DESI DR2.
canonical_node.action: The system should compute the chi-field prediction for H(z) using the given formula and compare it to observational data, specifically targeting the Hubble tension. It should also prepare for the Euclid 2026 falsification test.

plain_summary: This document describes a cosmological test of the chi-field framework, predicting a smooth sigmoid transition in the Hubble constant that could resolve the Hubble tension. It claims a 5 match with existing data and compatibility with DESI DR2, but does not provide the underlying derivation or statistical evidence. The prediction is falsifiable and will be tested by Euclid in 2026. Currently, it is a promising but unverified hypothesis.
